# CLI 0.0.8 evidence

Fresh captures from the optimized default-feature CLI, separate from the archived
0.0.7 and 0.0.4 recordings. No release publication is performed by these scripts.

- `demos.json`: version, binary SHA-256, Rust source/manifests/lock SHA-256, worktree
  provenance, complete command arguments, exit statuses and ANSI/media hashes.
- `recordings.zip`: 24 actual PTY ANSI/asciinema captures and two HTML exports.
- `asymmetric.png`: deterministic 3 × 3 asymmetric source generated by the script.
- `demo.toml`: profile-before-defaults fixture used for configuration inspection.
- `benchmark.json`: deterministic input recipe/hashes, serial/jobs-2/jobs-4 raw
  samples, arguments, reports, exit statuses and byte-identical export hashes.

## Reproduce

```sh
cargo build --release -p rs-rich-cli --locked
python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements-docs-media.txt
python scripts/capture_v8_demos.py --binary target/release/rich
python scripts/bench_batch.py --binary target/release/rich
```

The capture requires a POSIX PTY, FFmpeg and DejaVu fonts. There are nine anchors
in each of two viewport aspect ratios, dry-run then jobs-2 HTML export, and four
configuration commands. Completed output is held for two seconds with added
command captions; the terminal text itself is not synthesized. Wide and tall
viewports expose both crop axes, because cover crops only one axis at a time.

The dry-run capture checks that it creates no files before the export runs. The
benchmark checks exit status, success reports, output count and exported HTML
hashes on every warmup and measured run. Jobs order rotates between rounds.
Five measured rounds follow one warmup round for each jobs count; twelve JSON
files each contain 120 generated records. Timings include process startup,
rendering and disk writes, use warm filesystem caches, and were measured on a
shared host. They are observations, not a promised speedup. Temporary paths in
arguments record the exact historical invocation; scripts regenerate them.

Git HEAD identifies the base checkout; the source digest identifies the actual
working-tree Rust sources used for the build. Capture scripts and documentation
are intentionally outside that Rust source digest. Re-running replaces the
current evidence and regenerates temporary paths and timings.

## Captured timings

| Jobs | Median | Minimum | Maximum |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 58.2 ms | 54.6 ms | 70.8 ms |
| 2 | 71.8 ms | 66.9 ms | 72.3 ms |
| 4 | 36.3 ms | 35.8 ms | 41.1 ms |

The two-worker result is slower than serial for this small workload. More workers
do not imply proportional throughput; use the raw samples and remeasure for
your inputs. All 18 invocations exited 0 and produced the same twelve HTML files.

## Validation

`validation.json` and accompanying logs record 554 all-feature workspace tests,
119 lean CLI tests, 33 release regression tests, Clippy, Rust 1.90, docs,
terminal/watch/pager checks, snapshots and staged package verification. Golden
fixtures regenerated with rich 15.0.0 without changes. Remote CI is recorded on
the release PR; these local results do not claim publication.
